headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: shared git/workspace plus Replit secrets and broad egress create dangerous default interactions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aider reads and writes git-tracked files and shares state via a shared git repo; Replit Agent reads/writes Repl workspace files. That creates a plausible file-based bridge where malicious content from one agent can be treated as instructions by the other. No MCP or clipboard bridge is documented, so this is not high.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or workspace files, injected instructions can cross from one agent to the other.
IF either agent parses file contents as trusted task text, prompt injection becomes actionable.
mitigations: Use separate repos/workspaces for the two agents.
Add a human review step before either agent consumes files written by the other.
Prefix untrusted files with a quarantine naming convention and exclude them from agent inputs.
Disable automatic ingestion of generated markdown or task files.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to files and reject untrusted instruction-bearing content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aider handles model provider API keys via env vars and broad network egress; Replit Agent handles Replit Secrets and third-party API keys, and its workspace persists across sessions. If they share a workspace or repo, sensitive code or secrets can flow into outputs and then out over network calls. The blast radius includes secrets and source code, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF the same repository or workspace contains secrets or deployment configuration, both agents can access them.
IF either agent sends file contents to its backend or external APIs, those secrets can leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Move secrets out of shared files and into dedicated secret stores.
Split sensitive and non-sensitive work into separate repos/workspaces.
Rotate any keys exposed to either agent during joint use.
Review recent diffs for accidental secret inclusion before syncing.
requires-engineering: enforce secret redaction before model submission.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can execute shell commands, write files, and modify git state. Aider explicitly uses git commits and Replit Agent operates in a persistent Repl filesystem. If pointed at the same repo, concurrent writes and git mutations can overwrite each other or corrupt history without locking, matching the high-risk overlap rubric.
conditions: IF both agents edit the same branch or directory concurrently, file and git conflicts can occur.
IF no external locking or merge discipline exists, one agent can overwrite the other's changes.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate branch.
Serialize edits with a simple turn-taking rule.
Run git status before and after each agent turn.
Keep one agent read-only while the other writes.
requires-engineering: add workspace locking or transactional merge coordination.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aider produces code changes and git commits, while Replit Agent can act inside a Repl with user checkpoints and broad tool access. If Replit consumes Aider's output as authoritative, a mistaken patch or hallucinated fact can cascade into committed code or deployed changes. The downstream action authority makes the blast radius high.
conditions: IF Replit Agent uses Aider-generated diffs or instructions without independent verification, errors propagate.
IF either agent is allowed to commit or deploy based on the other's output, the cascade becomes operational.
mitigations: Require a human review of Aider output before Replit acts on it.
Ask Replit Agent to re-derive critical changes from source files, not from summaries.
Limit deployment permissions during joint sessions.
Use tests as a gate before accepting generated code.
requires-engineering: add automated verification between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Replit Agent explicitly touches secrets and deployment configuration in a cloud Repl, while Aider handles source code and git history locally. If regulated data or EU PII is placed in the shared workspace, Replit's cloud handling and third-party API calls can create residency or retention mismatches. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so uncertainty pushes upward.
conditions: IF regulated data, PHI, or EU PII is stored in the shared workspace, compliance obligations may be triggered.
IF the deployment or model-provider region is not contractually aligned with the data class, residency risk exists.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace.
Use synthetic or masked data for joint sessions.
Confirm vendor DPAs and residency settings before use.
Restrict joint sessions to non-sensitive codebases.
requires-engineering: document and enforce data-class routing rules.
